frontmatter.title: Decoded quantum interferometry
frontmatter.description: An executed fixed decoded-quantum-interferometry circuit and portable public companion, with explicit larger-family and physical-resource limits.

children.value: Decoded quantum interferometry (DQI) connects optimization to coding theory: a Fourier transform turns a coherently decoded state into an objective-biased distribution. Jordan and colleagues introduced it in
. It is a separate optimization approach alongside QAOA and adiabatic evolution.
Implementation status: executed default, structured degree-one family and finite graph degree-two component; general families and physical accounting planned

Our original nine-wire default circuit passed 63 focused CPU tests and coherent checks of preparation, all 512 decoder basis mappings, cleanup and final amplitudes. The portable public notebook has also executed with a standard Python kernel: four cells completed on Linux with locked Python 3.12.14 on 13 November 2026 (3.074 seconds recorded before the final guard seal). Its cells check saved facts and file bindings and present the original figure; this later notebook run does not repeat the earlier quantum simulation.

These are separate evidence events. The earlier combined circuit-and-notebook attempt stopped after 58.014051583 seconds with its notebook incomplete. Its complete circuit/export component remains valid; completion of the new public companion does not rewrite that earlier outcome. The separate structured degree-one implementation is described below. A

now has an accepted finite C5 component and a separately executed saved companion, with a figure-eight export kept generation-only. Arbitrary DQI matrices and growing-degree families, rotation synthesis, general physical accounting and local formal proof remain planned. No hardware experiment or generic optimization advantage is claimed.

Hamiltonian Decoded Quantum Interferometry for General Pauli Hamiltonians
by Bu, Gu and Li is a planned variant, identified by the primary

decoded quantum interferometry. Its abstract discusses mixed-state preparation shaped by a chosen polynomial of a general Pauli Hamiltonian, assuming access to an appropriate decoding oracle. The polynomial describes the prepared state, not an unconditional polynomial-time guarantee. No local HDQI oracle or circuit has been implemented, and our binary default decoder does not validate that oracle assumption.
Planned OPI, decoder and streaming extensions

children.label: Planned OPI, decoder and streaming extensions

children.value: preprint versions; peer-reviewed successors are unverified

. They are planned extensions here, with relevant manuscript passages read but no local implementation or physical-resource comparison. The bibliography records exact versions and bounded successor checks.
Rosmanis’s version 1 improves optimal polynomial intersection (OPI) preparation and decoding under an explicit memory model

. Section 2 distinguishes quantum access to classical memory (QRAMC) from addressable quantum memory (QRAMQ). A nearly-linear runtime in that model still requires input loading, addressable workspace, reversible decoding, cleanup and readout. Those operations need concrete implementations and costs before comparison with an ordinary circuit or a fault-tolerant architecture; this result does not supply an estimate for our nine-wire example.
Apte and colleagues’ version 2 analyzes nonbinary cycle codes and imperfect decoding for fixed targets

. Worst-case minimum distance and recovery under DQI’s error distribution are different guarantees. The paper’s regular-graph comparisons concern specified fields, noise distributions and classical decoder classes. Keep those regimes attached to its results: they neither establish general DQI advantage nor constitute a blanket dequantization of the Nature paper’s distinct OPI construction.

The bounded materializer has a nine-wire/512-operation ceiling; the coherent simulator has separate 512-amplitude and 512-dimensional operator limits. The original CPU workload used a 32 MiB quantum ndarray contract and a 1 MiB evidence/export cap. Its NumPy-domain boundary observations were at most 8,388,608 bytes, backed by a pinned sequential-buffer analysis below 17 MiB. These observations are not total process RSS or a universal allocator-peak measurement. No dense matrix is exported.

Full physical accounting for this original default still requires arbitrary-RY synthesis and coherent approximation allocation, routing, actual scalable decoder workspace, code/factory/reset/readout/control costs, input delivery, classical scoring and the chosen quality/confidence repetition budget. No Native or factory estimate for this default has executed; the structured degree-one family’s conditional resource evidence is separate. Future comparisons must hold the problem, requested accuracy, success and physical assumptions fixed against the frozen surface-code baseline.

adds a real weight-two shell, a clean two-error decoder and inline source/verification accounting. Its C5 code is affine/repetition-equivalent and has a linear classical optimum; no generic output-success or optimization-advantage claim follows. General matrices, growing-degree bias and complete physical comparisons remain planned. They need real correctable-weight/decoder promises, specified input and field representations, explicit reversible preparation/decoder/workspace construction, and matching synthesis, repetitions, readout/scoring and physical accounting. The implemented structured family’s all-zero assignment is an immediate classical optimum, so it supplies no optimization advantage claim. A bigger truth table alone is not an efficient general decoder. No local DQI theorem or Hamiltonian HDQI oracle has been reproduced.

The implementation, explanation and figure are original MIT work. The coherent record identifies Python 3.12.14, Qiskit 2.6.2 (Apache-2.0), NumPy 2.5.4 and exact source/environment hashes. The public companion and generator have their own source identities; their adaptation does not change the recorded coherent validation.
